Figure 2:Full-context two-step dubbing architecture.Masked source frames
and a reference image preserve speaker appearance and pose, target-audio tokens
drive lip articulation, and bidirectional self-attention jointly denoises the
complete latent window in two steps.

Figure 3:Three-stage training and distillation pipeline.Top: full-context teacher training via audio warm-up, joint editing adaptation, and
replacement-aware refinement. (a) Replacement-aware training masks out source-mouth
reconstruction under unpaired speech. (b) Guided trajectory regression distills the
48-step CFG-guided teacher into a two-step student. (c) Distribution matching
distillation recovers visual realism in the final two-step model.

Figure 6:Held-out multilingual examples.Twelve mechanically selected cases
(six English and six Chinese) are shown at matched times. Rows contain the source,
same-audio edit, and replacement-speech edit; insets enlarge the mouth, and green
borders identify replacement-speech outputs.

Figure 7:Streaming implementation validation.A four-step
checkpoint generates a real continuous 10-second HDTF chain with one persistent
bounded cache, overlapping long-audio Whisper features, and streaming VAE state.
The absolute cache endpoint reaches 65 latent frames while retained KV saturates at
22 (one reference plus 21 video frames). TTFF is 1.16s and peak allocated memory is
23.04GiB. Official SyncNet evaluation in two independent five-second windows gives
Sync-C/D10.086/6.40710.086/6.407and9.719/6.7259.719/6.725, with zero offset in both windows; thus the
persistent cache has zero measuredoffsetdrift in this interface test.
The later 60-second audit exposes lower-face collapse despite stable synchronization.
The measured end-to-end system RTF is 5.97.
